description:
Check every number in a draft against the filing characters it cites, and link them.

Write your draft with a citation right after each figure, using the ref that
list_figures or verify_figure gave for it:
    revenue of $68.1 billion [ref:0001045810-26-000019/q4fy26pr.htm@112+4]
For a number you calculated, state the formula, then cite its inputs; a, b, c… are
the refs in the order you cite them:
    up 73% [calc: a/b-1, ref:<current>, ref:<prior>]
    free cash flow margin 53.9% [calc: (a-b)/c, ref:<operating cash flow>, ref:<capex>, ref:<revenue>]
Formulas use a-h, + - * /, parentheses and constants (a*4, a/b*100). A measure such
as a margin can be defined more than one way, so the formula you state is the one
checked and shown (formula_source "stated"); a figure printed in parentheses is tried
as negative, then as a positive amount (signs). Without a formula, the usual sum,
difference, ratio and growth rate are tried (formula_source "inferred").
You may also give a calc's value: [calc: 53.9% = (a-b)/c, ref:…]; without it, a calc is
for the number just before the bracket. A ref is for the number in its sentence that
equals the characters it points at, wherever it sits, so a ref at the end of a
sentence works, and a year is checked like any figure when the ref points at a year.
A ref names the exact characters in the document: <accession>/<filename>@<start>+<len>.

Returns per citation: ok / rounded (your number is the cited figure times a power of
ten, rounded), mismatch (the cited characters, or your formula of them, give a different
number), bad_ref (no number at that position), bad_formula (unreadable, or not using
every cited input), bad_claim (a calc's stated value is not in its sentence), not_derivable (no formula stated, and no sum, difference, ratio
or growth rate of the inputs gives your number). unsourced_numbers lists figures with no citation. Fix
every failure before presenting the text, then use linked_text and footnotes: each
footnote links to the highlighted figure in the filing, so a reader can check it.

Args:
    text: The draft, with [ref:…] / [calc: …] citations (max ~200 KB)
name: check_citations
title: Check Citations in a Draft
